title: Catalog
description: Per-provider domain knowledge. This is not an icon table: it is where we decide, resource type by resource type, which reference means 'lives inside'. Terraform has no concept of containment, so the nesting the product draws is a decision recorded here. One file, two consumers -- the Go analyzer applies the rules, the interface reads the presentation.

type.description: The Terraform resource type this entry describes.

category.description: Comparable across providers on purpose, so a learner can see that a VPC and a VNet play the same role.

icon.description: Path within the icon set, without extension.

isContainer.description: Whether other resources are drawn inside this one.

parentRules.description: Which attribute makes this resource a child of another, in priority order. For an aws_instance, subnet_id beats vpc_id: the more specific placement wins.

edgeRules.description: Which references earn a drawn connection. Deliberately few: drawing every dependency produces the unreadable tangle this product exists to avoid.

labelTemplate.description: How the node is labelled. Supports {{name}} and attribute references.

priority.description: Lower wins. Ties are a catalog bug and the tests reject them.

kind.description: traffic: something sends requests to something else. data: something reads or writes something else. control: something governs something else.

show.description: False records the relationship in the model without drawing it. Security group wiring is real and useful to query, and ruinous to draw.
